terms.meaning: One of 10 equal parts of a unit, written 1/10 or 0.1.
One of 10 equal parts of a tenth, written 1/100 or 0.01.
The mark between the units and the tenths. Places to its right show tenths, hundredths and thousandths.

items.name: Places around the point
items.formula: Each place is 10 times the place on its right

items.name: Reading decimals
items.formula: Say each digit after the point
items.example: 7.05 is seven point zero five: 7 units and 5 hundredths.

items.name: Comparing decimals
items.example: 4.27 is more than 4.195, because 2 tenths is more than 1 tenth.

items.name: Zeros at the end
items.formula: They do not change the value

items.name: Decimal number patterns
items.example: 4.4, 4.8, 5.2, 5.6: add 0.4 each time, so 6.0 comes next.

items.name: Estimating a sum
items.formula: The sum lies just above the sum of the whole parts
items.example: 25.936 + 8.202 is more than 25 + 8 = 33 and less than 26 + 9 = 35.

mistakes.text: More digits does not mean a bigger decimal. 0.5 is more than 0.123.
7.05 is not 7.5. The 0 keeps the 5 in the hundredths place.
Line up the points, not the last digits. 2.5 + 1.25 = 3.75, not 1.50.
